newsitem.title: DENMARK: Profit-taking could slow Danish shares' rush ahead.
newsitem.headline: Profit-taking could slow Danish shares' rush ahead.

text.p: Danish share prices stormed to fresh records on Tuesday but dealers said that profit-taking could slow, although not neccessarily stop, further progress.
"The recent big price rises may soon bring profit-taking to the market, we have already seen some today with Novo Nordisk, Carlsberg and the banks," a dealer said.
The KFX top-20 index closed up 1.20 point to 128.82, in overall bourse turnover of 1.018 billion crowns, after earlier touching 129.20.
It was a new life-high, the 11th in 12 trading days.
The KFX October future rose 0.85 point to 128.70.
"The price rises are a little too sharp for the moment, but if we do not see a correction soon there are no limits to how high we can go," the dealer said.
Novo Nordisk peaked at 990 crowns but profit-taking toward the end of the day sent it back to a still respectable 980, 14 crowns up on Monday's close, with 118,000 shares traded.
Carlsberg finished eight crowns up at 385 crowns and Den Danske Bank closed seven crowns better off at 437.
Among the losers were EAC, down three crowns to 122, and Copenhagen Airports which came down one crown to 621 crowns.
